stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Slide $U_{max}$ and $f$ to shape the AC voltage $u(t) = U_{max}\,\sin(2\pi f\,t)$. Complete at least one full period to advance.
stages.concept: Alternating voltage oscillates between $+U_{max}$ and $-U_{max}$ with period $T = 1/f$. A multimeter reads the effective value $U_{eff} = U_{max}/\sqrt{2}$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Overlay your live curve on the dashed target: tune $U_{max}$ and $f$ until both match within tolerance.
stages.concept: Peak-to-peak $= 2\,U_{max}$. Period $T$ is the horizontal distance between two consecutive maxima. Frequency $f = 1/T$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Only the target curve is drawn. Read $U_{max}$ from its peak and $f$ from its period, set the sliders, then press RUN.
stages.concept: Method: measure peak height $\Rightarrow U_{max}$. Measure time between two peaks $\Rightarrow T$, then $f = 1/T$. Verify with $U_{eff} = U_{max}/\sqrt{2}$.

labels.peek_hint: peak height gives U_max; time between two peaks gives T, then f = 1/T
labels.tip1: slide U_max and f — watch peaks, valleys, and the effective value U_eff
labels.tip2: match dashed target: adjust U_max for peak height, f for peak spacing
labels.tip3: read U_max from the peak and T from peak spacing, compute f = 1/T, press RUN

1.1: Move both sliders — watch how U_max scales the peaks and f squeezes the period.
1.2: The dashed lines at +U_max and -U_max are envelopes. The dashed line at U_eff = U_max/sqrt(2) marks what a multimeter reads.
1.3: One full period is one crest + one trough. Wait until the sim clock passes t = T = 1/f.

2.1: The target's peak height is your U_max. Adjust the U_max slider first.
2.2: Count how many periods fit in the visible window; each period is T = 1/f wide.
2.3: Fine-tune f last — small f changes shift many peaks visibly.

3.1: Look at the target: what is the highest value it reaches? That is U_max.
3.2: Find two consecutive peaks on the target. The horizontal distance is T. Then f = 1/T.
3.3: Press Peek for the reading method. Set U_max and f, then RUN.
